title: Profile of Victims of Internet Love Scams
what_it_is: Profile of Victims of Internet Love Scams

sections.label: Internet Love Scam victims
sections.summary: Many Internet Love Scam victims are females aged 30 to 60, befriended by scammers on social media and dating platforms before being cheated of money.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: A significant proportion of victims of Internet Love Scams are female and between 30 and 60 years old.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The scammers mainly befriend their victims through social media and dating platforms, such as Facebook, Instagram, Tinder and OkCupid, winning their trust over time before cheating them of their money.

sections.label: Transnational Commercial Crime Task Force
sections.summary: The Police set up the TCTF in October 2017 to tackle transnational Internet Love Scams, seizing over $1 million and closing about 300 money mule bank accounts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In October 2017, the Police set up the Transnational Commercial Crime Task Force (TCTF), which will also look into tackling transnational Internet Love Scams.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Since its formation, TCTF has seized more than $1 million and closed around 300 bank accounts belonging to money mules who were involved in such scams.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This has led to a steady decline in reports of such scams from about 100 cases in September 2017, to about 40 in February 2018.

sections.label: Recovering seized scam money
sections.summary: The TCTF seized more than $1 million and closed about 300 bank accounts, and the Police will apply to the Courts to recover the money for rightful owners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: On the question of how much money has been recovered, as I mentioned just now, TCTF has seized more than $1 million and closed about 300 bank accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: The Police will apply to the Courts to ensure that the money gets recovered to the rightful owners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: As a result, despite the Police's best efforts, it may be difficult to retrieve the money and return it to the rightful owners.
